title: Rotate a VCF Automation named credential without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
Our VCF Automation provider deployment (VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1) needs automated rotation of the secret behind the named credential that our production vCenter registration authenticates with. Security wants that secret changed on a schedule. Operations will not sign off, because the last manual rotation killed requests that were already running against that vCenter.

This repository is where that tooling lives.

`docs/contract.json` is the contract for the VCF Automation Provider Infrastructure APIs we speak. VCF Automation publishes no machine-readable API specification, so the contract was transcribed by hand from Broadcom's xAPIs reference pages; `docs/official_sources.json` records each source page, the operation it documents and the fetch date. Treat the contract as authoritative for this repo but descriptive rather than normative: where it carries a `notDocumented` note, the reference was silent, so do not invent something to fill the gap. The contract explicitly labels the conservative safety assumption used for in-place secret updates rather than presenting it as reference text. `vcfa_mock.py` is a loopback mock pinned to the contract and serves only the operations the contract names.

Implement the two stubbed modules:

- `vcfa_rotate/client.py` — a client for the operations the contract names. Each request must go on the wire in exactly the shape the contract describes. Read `wireRules` closely: an optional body field or query parameter the caller did not set must leave no trace in the request at all — not `null`, not an empty string, list or object — while an option the caller did set must survive to the wire even when its value is falsy. `None` is the existing signatures' not-supplied sentinel; other explicitly supplied falsy values, including `False`, `0`, `""`, `[]` and `{}`, must survive. Required parameters that have documented defaults still get sent.

- `vcfa_rotate/rotation.py` — `rotate_named_credential(...)`, which rotates the secret so that no request already in flight against the vCenter is ever left holding a secret the service no longer accepts. Two operations in the contract can cause exactly that in this repository's safety model; their `hazard` notes distinguish the documented delete behavior from the conservative in-place-update assumption. Order the work, and wait on the right reads, so that neither one does. The service will not refuse a rotation that strands live work — it will simply strand it — so correctness here is about sequencing, not about handling an error.

Constraints:

- Python 3.10+ standard library only. No third-party packages.
- Do not modify `tests/`, `vcfa_mock.py`, or anything under `docs/`.
- Keep the public signatures already present in the stubs; they are called as documented.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` must pass.
deliverable: A working stdlib-only implementation of vcfa_rotate/client.py and vcfa_rotate/rotation.py.

verification.notes: All traffic goes to a loopback mock started inside the test process. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. The mock's state transitions are driven by request counts rather than wall-clock time, so the suite gives the same result on every run.
